mainEvent.title: Wed 11/18 · Fed minutes and Anthropic's pricing, after Nvidia's beat
mainEvent.body: Nvidia beat after Tuesday's close: revenue **$115.8B** (+103%) vs about $109B expected, non-GAAP EPS **$2.68** vs about $2.47, and a January-quarter outlook of **$130B ±3%** (including an extra week) vs about $125B (company release, CoinDesk). Shares were up about 3% before Wednesday's open, lifting Nasdaq futures; Chairman Harvey Jones said on the call the board does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang. Wednesday brings the **FOMC minutes at 2:00p** (Oct 27–28 meeting, two members favored a hike), Fed Governor Waller floating a 50bp December hike this morning, Target and Lowe's beating but slipping and TJX up about 6% before the open, Palo Alto after the close, and Anthropic's record IPO pricing after the close ahead of Thursday's Nasdaq debut. Walmart reports Thursday at 7:00a.

stories.title: Nvidia beats and guides to $130B; board shuts the door on Huang.
stories.body: Nvidia's fiscal Q3 revenue rose 103% to **$115.8B** (data center $107.6B, +110%) vs about $109B expected, with non-GAAP EPS of **$2.68** vs about $2.47 and a non-GAAP gross margin of 74.9%. It guided the January quarter to **$130B ±3%**, a 14-week quarter, vs about $125B, with gross margins of 71–72% and no China data-center sales assumed (company release, CoinDesk, TheStreet). The stock closed −0.4% at $155.46 and rose as much as about 3% after hours before settling up about 1–2% by 5:15p, and was up about 3% before Wednesday's open (Reuters, CoinDesk); the board also added $150B to the buyback (Newsquawk). Earlier Tuesday Jensen Huang said he would be "honored" to return as CEO if asked, but Chairman Harvey Jones said on the call the board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate him (CoinDesk); the WSJ reported the SEC is looking at whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors (via TheStreet). Polymarket (last trades Monday) gives about 13% that Huang rejoins by Dec 31 and 20% that a permanent CEO is named by then, with Arm's Rene Haas the favourite at about 28%.

stories.title: Selloff deepens: Dow sheds 849 points as software slides.
stories.body: The S&P 500 fell 1.03% to 7,340.53 Tuesday, the Nasdaq 0.74% to 24,328.38 and the Dow 848.75 points (1.64%) to 50,759.42, after Monday's tech rout; the Russell 2000 lost about 1.5%. The Nasdaq was down as much as about 2.1% intraday, and MarketWatch says the three major indexes touched their lowest levels in at least four months. Software led the losses: Salesforce −9.6% to $194.20, Intuit −7.1% (it reports Thursday), ServiceNow −6.8% and C3.ai −6.9% (24/7 Wall St). All 11 sector ETFs fell, and the VIX rose 11.1% to 25.46. Bright spots: Arm +4.0%, Broadcom +2.5%, SELLAS more than doubled on Phase 3 data, and AECOM +11%.

stories.title: Anthropic's record IPO is set to debut Thursday.
stories.body: Anthropic is expected to price Wednesday night and start trading on Nasdaq Thursday under the ticker ANT. It is selling 825 million shares at $70–78, up to about $64.4B, plus a $26B concurrent private placement (Nvidia and Google about $10B each), for about $90B in all (Bloomberg) at a valuation of up to about $1.4 trillion; the book is reported about six times oversubscribed, and Bloomberg reports Anthropic told investors it expects to price at the top of the range or higher, with multiple orders of $10B or more (via TradingKey). It would be the largest listing ever, and Bank of America's CEO says it is pushing some smaller listings into 2027. Polymarket prices a listing by Nov 19 at about 97%.

stories.title: Waller floats a 50bp hike ahead of Wednesday's Fed minutes.
stories.body: Fed Governor Waller said Wednesday morning that inflation is moving in the wrong direction and broadening, and that the Fed could respond by raising rates **50bp** in December or by signalling more tightening (TokenPost, Bloomingbit). That cuts against New York Fed President Williams, who said Tuesday policy will probably need one more increase but nothing "dramatic" (Bloomberg, Yahoo Finance). Data are mixed: October housing starts jumped 9.9% to **1.309M** vs about 1.24M expected, but permits fell 7.4% to 1.295M vs 1.38M (CoinDesk, Reuters via Rallies), after Tuesday's 0.4% drop in industrial production and an NAHB index of 25, the lowest since April 2012. Wednesday's 2:00p minutes cover the Oct 27–28 meeting, where the Fed held at 3.75–4.00% with two members favoring a hike. CME FedWatch was at 93.7% for a 25bp December hike Monday afternoon (Reuters); Kalshi and Polymarket are at about 91–92%.

stories.title: Target and Lowe's beat on tariff refunds but slip; TJX jumps.
stories.body: Target earned **$2.65** a share vs about $2.07 expected, including a $0.50 tariff refund, on sales of $27.07B (+7.1%, est $26.5B) with comparable sales up 5.6%, its fastest growth in five years, and raised its full-year EPS outlook to $10.65–11.40; the stock was down about 3.5% before the open (company release, RTTNews, Investing.com). Lowe's earned **$3.10** adjusted vs about $2.89, helped by $0.34 of tariff refunds, on sales of $22.76B (+9.3%) and comps of +1.8%; it lifted its sales outlook to about $92.5B but trimmed its margin outlook, and shares fell about 2.5% pre-market (company release, Securities.io, Startup Fortune). TJX matched at **$1.34** with sales of $15.95B vs $15.82B and comps +4%, now expects full-year comps of +4%, and rose about 6% (Reuters, Investing.com). Home Depot and Disney beat Tuesday but fell. Still to come: Palo Alto after Wednesday's close; Walmart Thursday at 7:00a (about $0.63–0.64 on roughly $187B), with Ross, Gap and Intuit (Polymarket 95% to beat $2.46) after Thursday's close and BJ's Friday.

stories.title: Oil edges up as Gulf attacks continue.
stories.body: WTI rose 0.3% to settle at **$86.01** and Brent 0.8% to **$93.14** Tuesday, recovering a little of Monday's 3% drop as attacks on shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz continued: Tehran targeted Bahrain for the third time in under a week, and a US official said US warplanes struck an Iranian missile site on Qeshm Island (Bloomberg via Rigzone). Supply is the offset: the IEA sees a surplus of about 2 million barrels a day this quarter and Goldman Sachs has flagged the risk of a glut next year. OPEC+ meets Nov 29 on 2027 policy.
